Sumit Mandoliya vs The State Of West Bengal & Ors on 5 June,
2025
June 05, 2025
 Ardr (63)

Wpa 12425 of 2025
 Sumit Mandoliya
 Vs.
 The State of West Bengal & ors.
 Adv. Arkadeb Biswas,
 Adv. Debarati Roy Chowdhury,
 ...for the petitioner.
 Adv. D. N. Maiti,
 Adv. Zoya Khanum,
 ...for the respondent nos. 3 & 4.
Adv. Swapan Banerjee, Adv. Biplab Guha, Adv. Dipendu Narayan Banerjee, Adv. Mohuya Dutta
Biswas, ...for the State.

1. Challenging the Memo dated 29th April, 2025 issued by the Principal, Raiganj Medical College,
Raiganj, Uttar Dinajpur, suspending the petitioner from the course, the present writ petition has been filed.
2. The petitioner claims to be a meritorious student and has qualified his secondary and senior secondary examinations.
Subsequently the petitioner has qualified in NEET UG for MBBS and was admitted in Raiganj Medical College, Raiganj, Uttar Dinajpur.
3. According to the petitioner, the petitioner has succeeded in the First Year MBBS examination which was held in November and December, 2023.

Insofar as the 2nd year MBBS examination is concerned which was held in December, 2024, the petitioner could not qualify in one (01) subject,
namely, Pathology and as such, intends to appear in the said paper by way of supplementary examination which is scheduled on 9th June, 2025 and 10th June, 2025.
4. In this context, Mr. Biswas learned advocate representing the petitioner has drawn attention of this Court to the examination schedule.

It is submitted that the petitioner is involved in a criminal proceeding and on basis of an FIR lodged against the petitioner by Tilak Marg Police Station, New Delhi being FIR no. 42 of 2024 dated 5th May, 2024 under Sections 419/420/468/471/34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 alleging that the petitioner had appeared on behalf of the some candidates in NEET examination by impersonating the actual candidate as well as there has been a mismatch in the admit card.

entities.text: Tilak Marg Police Station, New Delhi
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: The petitioner was however, able to secure a release order/bail as would corroborate from the order passed by the learned Additional Sessions Judge, New Delhi District New Delhi dated 3rd June, 2024.

entities.text: Additional Sessions Judge, New Delhi District New Delhi
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: According to the petitioner till date no charge sheet has been filed.

Unfortunately, all on a sudden without any show cause the suspension of the petitioner dated 29th Sumit Mandoliya vs The State Of West Bengal & Ors on 5 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/62577682/
1 April, 2025 has been issued which in effect, debars the petitioner from participating in MBBS examination scheduled on 9th and 10th June, 2025.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 5. Mr. Banerjee learned advocate appearing for the State would submit that today he is handicapped since the matter pertains to a police case in New Delhi and all relevant instructions are not available with him.
6. Mr. Maiti, learned advocate appearing for the University would submit that the order dated 29th April, 2025 has not been passed on the basis of any instructions issued by the University.

7. Having heard the learned advocates appearing for the respective parties and nothing that prima facie, the order impugned suspending the petitioner from MBBS Course had been issued without giving an opportunity of hearing to the petitioner and the same prima facie appears to have been issued on the basis of a direction issued by the National Medical Commission, Government of India,
New Delhi dated 15th April, 2025 which the parties could not produce, and also noting that same is based on external dictate without any application of mind, I am of the view that the petitioner is entitled to an interim order.

entities.text:
National Medical Commission, Government of India,
New Delhi

sentences.text: 8. It may be noted that the criminal proceeding may take years to complete.

9. As rightly pointed out by the learned advocate for the petitioner in a judgment delivered by a coordinate Bench of Rajasthan High Court in a batch of writ petitions, being WPA 8864 of 2025 on 23rd May, 2025 in the case of Vikas Vimani s/o Shri Krishna Ram vs. Controller of Examination Rajasthan University of Health Science, Jaipur, reported in 2025 : RJ - 1D 25240 the Hon'ble Rajasthan High Court in a similar set of circumstance was pleased to observe and record as follows:
"20.

entities.text: Vikas Vimani s/o Shri Krishna Ram vs. Controller of Examination Rajasthan University of Health Science, Jaipur
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: So far as petitioners" involvement in impersonating for other students is concerned, this Court does not deem it apt to dilate upon or to record any finding over such allegation.

Any discussion made or finding recorded herein may not be construed to be an observation or finding about petitioners' involvement in appearing for other candidates, because, for that purpose, the investigating agency and the trial court are the competent authority.
The adjudication made in this case is confined to the power and propriety of the University/NMC/college in suspending the petitioners and necessity or the justification for such action.

21. It is usual that the trial of the case takes years and in cases like the one in hands,
which involve allegations of impersonation and long list of witnesses, such possibilities becomes almost certainty.

22. So far as the provisions, which Mr. Siddharth Tatia has brought to the notice of the Court are concerned, they all relate to NMC's role and power of maintaining high standards, ethical or educational, about which no Court can have any sort of doubt.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Act of 2024, which deals with malpractices in public examination though provides for punishment but does not contain any provision for suspension.

24. There is a provision in the form of Regulation No.24 in the Regulations of 2021,
which provides for power to suspend in case of ragging.
But these regulations are confined to the cases of ragging and naturally, do not provide for suspension in the cases of impersonation.

25. So far as argument of Mr. Tatia based upon section 24 of the Act of 2019 and section 2(1)(a) of the Act of 2024 is concerned, according to this Court the petitioners do not fall within the ambit of candidate, because it is indicative of the candidate and a person, who appears for a candidate as a scribe'.

The petitioners, who have impersonated on behalf of the candidate can neither be treated to a candidate nor can they be alleged to be scribes, because scribe is a person, who has been authorised by the examining body to appear on behalf of the candidate.
whereas, the allegation against the petitioners is that they have impersonated the actual candidates and unauthorisedly rather fraudulently appeared in their place.
26. The petitioners would fall within the contours of a crime or organized crime as defined under sub- clause (h) of sub-section (1) of section 2 of the Act of 2024.

entities.text: sub- clause (h) of sub-section (1) of section 2
entities.label: PROVISION

sentences.text: They may also be treated to be persons associated with the service provider defined in sub- clause (i) of sub-section (1) of section 2 and sub- clause (v) of section 3 of the Act of 2024, but whether or not they really fall within the ambit and scope of these sections will ultimately based upon the evidence adduced by the prosecution and the finding recorded by the trial court in this regard.

entities.text: sub- clause (i) of sub-section (1) of section 2
entities.label: PROVISION

sentences.text: 27. Suspension usually presupposes initiation or contemplation of inquiry.

While,
observing that no inquiry has so far been initiated against the petitioners, this Court would like to add that even if the respondents so wish to propose, no inquiry is possible because the acts of impersonation were done outside the college(s) in which the petitioners are studying and because all the material, oral or occular evidence is with the police and not with the college(s).
Hence, even if an inquiry is conducted, it will be a futile exercise or a farce.
28. Hence, unless such finding is recorded and petitioners are held guilty, their future cannot be kept in suspended animation for indefinite period.

Had there been a case of the petitioners getting admission in the medical course by asking someone else to appear on their behalf, perhaps this Court would have not granted them any indulgence on the basis of sympathy or equitable consideration, because then their merit or eligibility itself was in doubt.
29. AIlegation against each of the petitioners herein is, that they have impersonated for other students in the NEET UG Examination.

However, so far as their own Sumit Mandoliya vs The State Of West Bengal & Ors on 5 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/62577682/
3 admission in medical colleges is concerned, there is no iota of allegation of getting admission fraudulently or by using unfair means -there is no quarrel about their merit and eligibility of getting admission in the medical courses.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 30. According to this Court, unless there is any statute or regulation, which provides for suspension, rustication or even ancellation of the admission impersonation in the examinations, the respondents cannot place the candidates involved in the petitioners under suspension.

31. If the suspension is allowed to continue, the loss would be irreversible and irreparable, inasmuch as the period which the criminal trial will take, the petitioners would not be able to continue with their studies and their future will be left in lurch.
And if, they are ultimately acquited, they would have lost 3- 4 precious years of their student life doing nothing.

32. This Court not even or a moment approves petitioners action of impersonation and firmly believes that looking to the increasing number of such cases, it is high time the Central Government brings appropriate legislation, but in absence of such legislation and without any power to suspend, placing the petitioners under suspension is not only ilegal, without jurisdiction, but also violative of their fundamental rights guaranteed under Article 19(1)(g) and 21 of the Constitution of India.
33.
The action on the part of the respondents in placing the petitioners under suspension is like holding them guilty and punishing them before the competent court convicts them.

34. But, since the allegation against the petitioners is, that they have appeared for other candidates in subsequent examination, this Court is persuaded to take somewhat lenient view, however, with caution and circumspection.
35. The writ petitions are, therefore, allowed.

36. The petitioners" suspension order(s) in each of the writ petitions are, hereby,
quashed.
Their suspension shall naturally be treated quashed from the date of order instant.
37. The respondent-college(s) shall forthwith allow them to attend classes.

In case,
petitioner fulfil the requisite attendance criteria, they shall be allowed to appear in the ensuing examination in accordance with law.

38. The petitioners shall be allowed to complete their course, but the respondents shall neither issue them degree nor shall they be registered, unless the trial is concluded and they are acquitted of the charges.

sentences.text:
In case, the petitioners are held guilty in the trial, the NMC shall be free to take appropriate decision in accordance with law, which may include even cancellation of their admission in the medical course."
10.

In view thereof, and for reasons noted hereinabove, I am of the view that the college authority should permit the petitioner to provisionally sit in Pathology Paper I and Pathology Paper II examinations which is scheduled on 9th and 10th June, 2025.
11. The order of suspension for the purpose of participation in the examination shall remain stayed.
12. It is made clear that the result of the petitioner's examination shall not be published without the leave of the Court.
13. The respondent authorities shall be at liberty to file affidavit in opposition to the writ petition on or before the matter is taken up.

14. List the matter before the regular Bench in the monthly list of July, 2025 subject to the convenience of the Hon'ble Court.
15.
All parties including the university are to act on a server copy of this order duly downloaded from the official website of this Court.

(Raja Basu Chowdhury, J)
